structured_facts.title: Okafor v St Aldhelm's Hospital NHS Trust

parties.name: St Aldhelm's Hospital NHS Trust
parties.description: Employer of Mr Graham Lyle, consultant spinal surgeon.

chronology.event: Mr Okafor consulted Mr Lyle about chronic neck pain radiating into his left arm.
Mr Okafor underwent cervical decompression surgery performed by Mr Lyle.

claims.claim: Claim damages in negligence for failure to warn of a material risk and alternative treatment before consent to surgery.

key_facts.text: On 2 February 2024, Mr Okafor consulted Mr Lyle about chronic neck pain radiating into his left arm.
Mr Lyle recommended cervical decompression surgery but did not mention a roughly 2% risk of nerve root damage or the alternative treatment of physiotherapy and steroid injections.
Mr Okafor informed Mr Lyle that his career depended on fine finger control of his left hand.
Mr Okafor signed a consent form and underwent surgery on 11 April 2024, which was performed with proper skill.
The risk of nerve damage materialized, causing permanent loss of fine motor control in two fingers of Mr Okafor's left hand, ending his professional career.
Mr Okafor says he would not have consented to surgery on that date if warned of the risk and would have tried physiotherapy and sought a second opinion, though he might have had surgery eventually.
The Trust relies on evidence that many responsible spinal surgeons in 2024 did not routinely mention the 2% risk and argues the surgery was not negligent, so failure to warn caused no loss.
Mr Okafor seeks damages for negligence based on failure to warn of material risk and alternative treatment before consenting to surgery.

objective.text: Mr Okafor wants to claim damages in negligence for the failure to warn him of a material risk and of the alternative treatment before he consented to surgery.
